video.title: How to Make Money With Tariffs While Everyone Panics

summary: Chris Koerner discusses business opportunities arising from the April 2025 US 'Liberation Day' tariffs. He pitches a sourcing-intelligence play using ImportYeti and Jungle Scout (sourcing agent, newsletter, cold outreach to Shopify stores), offshore staffing/placement agencies, a last-mile agency finishing AI-built (vibe-coded) projects, tariff consulting, buying distressed small businesses with seller financing, and made-in-America ecommerce. He also urges not to panic and cites companies founded in downturns. Mostly speculative brainstorming, not first-hand operator proof.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; solo episode

ideas.name: Tariff sourcing agent / alternative-factory finder for Shopify stores
ideas.one_liner: Find alternative non-tariffed manufacturers for brands' best-selling products using ImportYeti and charge a success fee or percentage of imports.
ideas.business_model: Success-based finder fee or broker percentage of imports
ideas.customer: US ecommerce brands (e.g. Shopify Plus stores) and companies importing from tariff-hit countries
ideas.problem: Tariffs make sourcing from China and other affected countries costlier; brands need alternative manufacturers
ideas.offer: Find better/alternative factories within 24 hours for three of the brand's products; paid only if the brand uses the supplier; or act as sourcing agent for a percentage of imports

pricing.notes: Only charge if the client ends up using the supplier found; broker's fee or finder fee as a percentage of everything imported; no figures stated

acquisition_channels.details: Scrape Shopify Plus stores with owner/exec contacts from BuiltWith (or have an Upwork VA do it for $20-50); email offering to find alternative manufacturers; list their three best sellers found via the /collections/all?sort_by=best-selling URL suffix; only do the work after they reply.

quote.text: you don't get to work until they respond to you because 95 plus% of people will never respond no matter how good your offer or email is
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Research on ImportYeti and Jungle Scout to find factories supplying similar products in less-affected countries, order samples to compare quality, and report alternatives to the client
unit_economics_claims: Upwork VA can scrape a list of Shopify stores for $20-50
95%+ of cold emails get no response
ideas.startup_cost: Low: ImportYeti account plus $20-50 for list scraping

acquisition.how: Lists and emails can be automated, but cold email to Shopify owners who are sole traders/individuals is restricted under UK PECR; targeting limited companies is allowed. Needs care.

onboarding.how: Agent can handle replies and collect the three products.

delivery.how: Agents can search ImportYeti-type data and shortlist factories, but supplier vetting and sample ordering need a human.

billing.how: Success-fee invoicing needs tracking of orders but is largely automatable.

support.how: Agent handles routine questions; negotiation escalates to a human.

uk_applicability.notes: Tariff framing is US-specific, but UK brands also seek supplier diversification. Cold email must target limited companies. ImportYeti covers US import data so UK brand coverage is weaker.

risks: Success-fee model means unpaid research effort
Clients may bypass you once they have the factory
Brands may not disclose actual purchases to verify fee

tactics.name: Find winning products then reverse-engineer their factories
steps: Pick a niche such as baby goods or kitchenware
Use Jungle Scout to find Amazon products with high sales and demand exceeding supply, checking recent trends
Search ImportYeti for the same or similar manufacturers
Look for manufacturers in countries less affected by tariffs
Order samples from them and from the incumbent to compare quality

quote.text: spend a couple hours one night finding random niche products that are selling like crazy
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Cold-email Shopify stores with their best sellers, work only after reply
steps: Export Shopify Plus store list with owner contacts from BuiltWith or pay an Upwork VA $20-50
Add the best-selling sort suffix to each store URL to see top products
Email stating you know their top three products and will find three alternative manufacturers at no cost
Only do the work once they reply, charge only if they use a supplier you find

quote.text: you don't get to work until they respond to you
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Do not wait to do the work for cold prospects: validate interest with a low-effort email first, since most never respond.

quote.text: Once they respond to you, then you get to work because you have a fish on the line.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Success-fee offers reduce buyer risk and can raise reply rates, at the cost of unpaid effort.
Niche audiences of buyers/executives can command ad rates far above audience size.
Software and digital businesses are insulated from physical tariffs and AI tools lower the build cost.
Gaps left by AI builders (unfinished projects) create service opportunities.
Market predictions are unreliable; avoid panic decisions.

quote.text: We're pretty terrible at predicting the future.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Information asymmetry plus seller financing lets buyers cover downside when acquiring in a downturn.
Crowded markets can still be worth entering if the industry is early in its long-term growth.
Simple expertise built through a few hours of AI research plus public content can position you as an expert when demand outstrips supply.

evidence_quality.rationale: Solo host brainstorm of speculative ideas with no first-hand results or verified numbers; most figures are hypothetical or hearsay. Historical company-founding anecdotes are loose.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes his own newsletter and podcast (tkopod.com); states ImportYeti mention is not an ad.
